summary: cfgzen ships a native dropper that fetches and stages a Windows payload on import
details: The package presents itself as a Rust-backed.env/config parser, but dotcfg/__init__.py unconditionally invokes _native.platform_check() at import time. The bundled _native.pyd is a PyO3/Rust binary that dynamically resolves WinHTTP and Winsock symbols (WSAStartup, WinHttpAddRequestHeaders, WinHttpSetOption), sets a Mozilla/5.0 Windows browser User-Agent, and issues HTTP(S) requests to files.catbox.moe/7t4wyu.<ext> — an anonymous file host with a history of malware staging. flate2/miniz_oxide is linked in to decompress the fetched blob. The same binary embeds host-identity environment variables (COMPUTERNAME, HOSTNAME, USERNAME, USER, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP) and an extensive CI-fingerprint list (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, TF_BUILD, BUILDKITE, DRONE, APPVEYOR, CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, TEAMCITY_VERSION, HEROKU_TEST_RUN_ID) reachable from the same code path as the network client, indicating recon and CI-gated triggering. Drop paths mimic legitimate Microsoft binaries (Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\EdgeUpdateService.exe, Microsoft\WindowsApps\RuntimeBroker_v2.exe, Microsoft\Edge\Temp\msedge_installer.exe, Microsoft\MediaSync\MediaSyncAgent.exe, Microsoft\Provisioning\ProvisioningHost.exe) with an envcorecache.dat staging filename, and a reversed string literal (uespemosarenegylmodnarodsetybdet — 'detbytesdodnaromlygenerasomepseu' reversed) is present as anti-scanner obfuscation. None of this has any legitimate relationship to parsing configuration files.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
